sourcedFrom: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet (UNKNOWN — no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: A sealed can on YHM's Phantom Q.D. mount, so this is maintenance rather than a teardown — the TURBO K body does not open and no interior disassembly is published. What you service is the mount: the Q.D. adapter into the back of the can at 35 ft-lbs, and the muzzle device onto the barrel at 20-30 ft-lbs. One warning before you read the book itself: YHM's greeting line in this PDF names the TURBO T2, not the TURBO K, and the first step below deals with that. Everything else in it — cover, spec panel, every instruction, the compatibility page — is TURBO K.

steps.title: Read the greeting line carefully — this PDF names two different models
steps.action: One line of this booklet is wrong and you should know which. The congratulations line greets you on a TURBO T2. Everything else in the document is TURBO K: the cover, the specification panel headed THE TURBO K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140, every install instruction, and the compatible-muzzle-devices page. YHM serves this same PDF from both its legacy Turbo K page and its legacy Turbo T2 page, and the greeting is stale text from the other product. Treat this as the Turbo K book, but if your can is engraved T2 rather than K, check the part number against YHM before relying on any figure here.
steps.prose: Seven Turbo K identifications against one T2 line. The two pages that actually title the document — the cover and the spec panel — are both Turbo K.
steps.quote: CONGRATULATIONS ON THE PURCHASE OF YOUR YHM® TURBO® T2 SUPPRESSOR!
steps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — greeting line, PDF p.3 (the booklet prints no folio on any page)
steps.warn: Check the engraving on your own can. Turbo K is YHM-2140; the K-RB is a different product on a different mount standard (YHM-2180, HUB) with its own manual.

steps.title: Firearm unloaded and pointed somewhere safe before the can is touched
steps.action: Clear the host first and keep the muzzle in a safe direction for the whole job. YHM puts this at the head of its removal and installation section, and mounting or dismounting a can is exactly when a muzzle gets swung across a room.
steps.quote: BE CERTAIN THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED AND THE MUZZLE IS POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION BEFORE STARTING THIS REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION PROCESS.
steps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — INSTALLATION AND USE, PDF p.5
steps.warn: Suppressed does not mean safe. YHM's own caution is that a suppressed firearm is just as dangerous as an unsuppressed one.

steps.title: This book covers the can, not your firearm
steps.action: There is no host-firearm procedure anywhere in these twelve pages. YHM routes the work on the gun to a gunsmith who knows your specific model, and how to clear and strip your rifle lives in that rifle's own manual, not this one.
steps.caution: Installing it wrong voids the warranty and, in YHM's words, removes any liabilities against the manufacturer.
steps.quote: ONLY A LICENSED GUNSMITH EXPERIENCED WITH YOUR MODEL OF FIREARM SHOULD INSTALL THIS PRODUCT.
steps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — INSTALLATION AND USE, PDF p.5

steps.title: Let it cool, then unscrew the can off the Q.D. mount
steps.action: Wait until the body is cool enough to hold, then unscrew it off the Phantom Q.D. mount. It comes off by hand — the Q.D. system is designed so that no tools are needed in either direction.
steps.prose: Heat is the reason to wait. Thirty rounds of automatic fire puts the tube 225°F above ambient and it stays hot well after the last shot.
steps.quote: TO REMOVE THE SOUND SUPPRESSOR SIMPLY UNSCREW FROM THE Q.D. MOUNT.
steps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — SUPPRESSOR, PDF p.7
steps.warn: THE SUPPRESSOR CAN CAUSE SEVERE BURNS AND IGNITE FLAMMABLE MATERIALS.

steps.title: Check the mount is still tight — every time, not once
steps.action: With the can off, check the Phantom Q.D. mount is still firm on the barrel and the adapter still tight in the back of the suppressor. Firing walks these joints loose and YHM asks for the check to be repeated, not done once at fitting. A loose can is a misaligned can.
steps.prose: It is the first entry on YHM's own list of what causes baffle strikes, ahead of poor barrel threads and poor ammunition.
steps.caution: IF INSTALLED AND USED ACCORDING TO THE SPECIFICATIONS WITHIN THIS BOOKLET, A BAFFLE STRIKE IS HIGHLY UNLIKELY.
steps.quote: IT IS POSSIBLE THAT WITH FIRING THE SUPPRESSOR MAY BECOME LOOSE, WHICH CAN CAUSE MISALIGNMENT.
steps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — NOTE, PDF p.3

steps.title: Wipe the outside down with a damp cloth
steps.action: Wipe oil, dirt and fouling off the outside of the tube with a damp cloth. That is the entire routine external service YHM publishes for this can — no solvent bath, no brushing, nothing abrasive on the cerakote.
steps.quote: EXCESS OIL, DIRT, AND OTHER CONTAMINANTS SHOULD BE WIPED FROM THE OUTSIDE SURFACE USING A DAMP CLOTH.
steps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — Care, PDF p.8

steps.title: Take the can off the rifle when you are done shooting
steps.action: Do not store it mounted. Condensation trapped inside is the most common problem YHM sees with suppressors, and taking the can off lets it evaporate. If it must stay on, store the rifle muzzle-down with the bolt open so the inside can drain and breathe.
steps.prose: The corrosion this prevents is happening on baffles you can never reach.
steps.aside: IF THE SOUND SUPPRESSOR IS TO REMAIN ON THE RIFLE, IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE RIFLE BE STORED IN A MUZZLE-DOWN POSITION WITH THE BOLT LEFT OPEN.
steps.quote: THE BEST WAY TO PREVENT CORROSION OF YOUR RIFLE IS TO REMOVE THE SUPPRESSOR AS SOON AS YOU ARE FINISHED SHOOTING.
steps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — Care, PDF p.8

steps.title: Nothing wet or loose goes inside the tube
steps.action: Never fire the can with water, gel, grease or anything else inside it. A suppressor with its volume filled is a pressure vessel, and YHM's stated consequence is damage to the can, damage to the host, or serious injury. It also voids the warranty outright.
steps.quote: DO NOT USE THIS SOUND SUPPRESSOR WITH WATER OR ANY OTHER MEDIA INSIDE THE SOUND SUPPRESSOR.
steps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — WARNING!, PDF p.3
steps.warn: If you have soaked the can, it must be fully drained and blown dry before it goes back on a rifle.

steps.title: That is the whole field strip — the body does not open
steps.action: Can off the mount, mount checked, outside wiped. No further disassembly of the TURBO K is published anywhere in the booklet: no baffle stack, no end cap, no core. Deep Clean covers the two joints that do come apart — the Phantom Q.D. adapter and the muzzle device — plus the solvent flush and the cleaning interval.
steps.prose: YHM's published interval for the inside is 2000 to 3000 rounds, and it says the internals rarely need doing at all.
steps.quote: AS A GENERAL RULE, WE RECOMMEND CLEANING THE SOUND SUPPRESSOR AFTER EVERY 2000 TO 3000 ROUNDS.
steps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — Care, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Phantom Q.D. adapter out of the back of the body
deepSteps.action: The adapter threads into the rear of the suppressor and is the only part of the can that separates from it. Grip the TURBO K body firmly, put the supplied wrench on the notches in the base of the adapter and back it out anticlockwise. Going back in it is hand-started to avoid cross-threading, then torqued clockwise to about 35 ft-lbs.
deepSteps.prose: Start the thread by hand every time. This is a proprietary mount and the adapter is not a part worth galling.
deepSteps.aside: THE PHANTOM® Q.D. ADAPTER (1B) ASSEMBLY INTO THE TURBO K SUPPRESSOR BODY (2B) BY HAND, TAKING CARE NOT TO CROSS-THREAD.
deepSteps.quote: HOLD THE TURBO® K BODY (2B) WITH A FIRM GRIP. USING THE SUPPLIED WRENCH (3B) TO GRASP THE NOTCHES IN THE BASE OF THE ADAPTER (1B), TIGHTEN THE ADAPTER IN A CLOCKWISE DIRECTION. TORQUE TO APPROXIMATELY 35 FT-LBS.
deepSteps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — PHANTOM® Q.D. ADAPTER, PDF p.5
deepSteps.warn: Adapter into the body: 35 ft-lbs. This is NOT the muzzle-device figure — see the next step.

deepSteps.title: Muzzle device on the barrel — 20-30 ft-lbs against a square shoulder
deepSteps.action: The Phantom Q.D. mount needs YHM's own matching muzzle device on the barrel. Fit it with a 3/4" open-end wrench, torque to 20-30 ft-lbs, and make sure it lands flat against a 90° barrel shoulder. If the mount needs clocking, use the shim kit that came with it.
deepSteps.prose: Two joints, two numbers: 35 ft-lbs for the adapter into the can, 20-30 ft-lbs for the device onto the barrel.
deepSteps.quote: IT IS ESSENTIAL THAT THE MUZZLE DEVICE SEATS AGAINST A 90° BARREL SHOULDER.
deepSteps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — MUZZLE DEVICE, PDF p.6

deepSteps.title: The crush washer goes in the bin, and is never replaced with another
deepSteps.action: Strip off whatever muzzle device is on the barrel now and throw the crush washer away with it. Do not fit a new crush or peel washer under a suppressor mount — YHM voids the warranty over this by name, because those washers do not compress evenly and what they leave is an off-axis mount.
deepSteps.prose: Indexing is done with the supplied shim kit instead. That is what it is in the box for.
deepSteps.quote: *CRUSH WASHERS WILL VOID THE WARRANTY AS THEY DO NOT CRUSH UNIFORMLY AND WILL CAUSE IMPROPER MOUNTING AND BAFFLE STRIKES.*
deepSteps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — MUZZLE DEVICE, PDF p.6
deepSteps.warn: A crush washer, a peel washer, or anything else that causes misalignment voids the warranty on both the can and the host.

deepSteps.title: Only YHM's listed devices carry this can
deepSteps.action: The compatibility page in the back of the booklet lists the muzzle devices that mate with the TURBO K: the YHM-3102's, the YHM-5M2-QD and the YHM-3102-1MB's. A device that is not on that page is not a Q.D. mount this suppressor is published to sit on.
deepSteps.aside: The K-RB book lists an entirely different set — YHM-4302's, YHM-4315's and YHM-3102-1MB's — which is one more reason not to read one book for the other.
deepSteps.quote: the TURBO® K COMPATIBLE MUZZLE DEVICES
deepSteps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — compatibility page heading, PDF p.9

deepSteps.title: Solvent flush — done through the can, never into it
deepSteps.action: The inside rarely needs anything. When it does, YHM's published method is to submerge the whole suppressor in a hydrocarbon-based gun cleaning solvent. There is no dismantling in this: the can goes in whole and comes out whole.
deepSteps.prose: Kroil, or one part transmission fluid to two parts mineral spirits, are the mixes YHM names.
deepSteps.quote: CLEANING OF THE INTERNALS IS RARELY NECESSARY BUT CAN BE ACCOMPLISHED BY SUBMERGING THE SUPPRESSOR IN A HYDROCARBON BASED GUN CLEANING SOLVENT (SUCH AS KROIL OR A MIXTURE OF 1 PART TRANSMISSION FLUID AND 2 PARTS MINERAL SPIRITS).
deepSteps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — Care, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Drain it, then blow it dry
deepSteps.action: Let all the solvent run out, then blow the remainder clear with high-pressure air before the can goes near a rifle. A suppressor still wet inside is the media-filled can the WARNING page rules out, and firing it that way is what raises pressures dangerously.
deepSteps.quote: ALLOW THE SOLVENT TO DRAIN OUT OF THE SUPPRESSOR AND BLOW OUT ANY REMAINING SOLVENT USING A HIGH PRESSURE AIR HOSE.
deepSteps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — Care, PDF p.8
deepSteps.warn: Do not shortcut the drying. Trapped solvent is trapped media.

deepSteps.title: Back on the mount until the ratchet stops
deepSteps.action: Slide the back of the body over the Phantom Q.D. mount until it stops, then turn it clockwise by hand. You will hear the locking mechanism click as it goes. Keep turning until the ratcheting stops — that, not a torque figure, is how you know it has sealed.
deepSteps.prose: No tools. If it needs tools to seat, something on the threads or the mount is dirty.
deepSteps.aside: TIGHTEN THE SOUND SUPPRESSOR FIRMLY UNTIL THE RATCHETING STOPS TO ENSURE A CORRECT SEAL.
deepSteps.quote: INSTALL THE TURBO® K BODY (2D) BY SLIDING THE BACK END OVER THE YHM® PHANTOM® Q.D. MOUNT (1D) UNTIL IT STOPS, THEN TURN THE SUPPRESSOR (2D) CLOCKWISE TO HAND TIGHTEN.
deepSteps.cite: THE TURBO® K SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2140 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — SUPPRESSOR, PDF p.7

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE OF THE TUBE
tasks: Wipe excess oil, dirt and other contaminants off the outside surface with a damp cloth
Let the can reach a temperature you can hold before touching it
Do not abrade the matte black high-temp cerakote finish

cleaning.name: MOUNT & THREADS
tasks: Clean the Phantom Q.D. mount and the rear of the body where they engage
Check the adapter is still tight in the back of the can — 35 ft-lbs
Check the muzzle device is still tight on the barrel — 20-30 ft-lbs against a 90° shoulder
Never fit a crush washer or peel washer under the mount; use the supplied shim kit to index
Use only the listed devices: YHM-3102's, YHM-5M2-QD, YHM-3102-1MB's

cleaning.name: INTERIOR — 2000 TO 3000 ROUNDS
tasks: Rarely necessary; when it is, submerge the whole can in a hydrocarbon-based gun cleaning solvent
Drain fully, then blow out the remaining solvent with high-pressure air
Never fire the can with water or any other media inside it
Do not attempt to open the body — no interior disassembly is published for the Turbo K

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Take the suppressor off as soon as you have finished shooting so condensation can evaporate
If it stays on, store the rifle muzzle-down with the bolt open

reassembly: Hand-start the Phantom Q.D. adapter into the rear of the TURBO K body, then torque it to approximately 35 ft-lbs with the supplied wrench on the notches in the adapter base.
Fit a listed YHM muzzle device to a clean barrel thread against a 90° shoulder, 20-30 ft-lbs with a 3/4" open-end wrench, using the shim kit — never a crush washer — to index it.
Slide the body onto the Q.D. mount until it stops, then turn clockwise by hand.
Keep tightening until the ratcheting stops; that is the correct seal.
Confirm the can is bone dry inside if it has been soaked, before it goes on the rifle.
fncheck: With the firearm confirmed unloaded, check the suppressor is firmly attached to both the firearm and the Phantom Q.D. adapter, and that the ratchet has stopped. Anything that moves, rattles or will not seat comes back off — YHM lists the suppressor coming loose from the host as the number one cause of baffle strikes, ahead of poor barrel threads, incorrect mount installation and poor ammunition. Re-check the same joints periodically during shooting, not only before it.
